canh-bap-cai-thit-vien.name: Cabbage and Pork Meatball Soup
aliases: Vietnamese Cabbage Soup with Pork Meatballs
Cabbage Soup with Minced Pork Balls
canh-bap-cai-thit-vien.serving_basis: One pot for four people at a family meal.
canh-bap-cai-thit-vien.description: Sweet cabbage simmers with pork meatballs and carrot in a light broth. It pairs well with braised fish or meat.
canh-bap-cai-thit-vien.finished_dish: A clear, mild broth with tender cabbage, juicy meatballs and carrot slices.
canh-bap-cai-thit-vien.serving: Serve hot with scallions and steamed rice.
tips: Mix pork and pork paste until cohesive.
Add meatballs to a gentle boil and skim the broth.
Add cabbage near the end so it stays tender, not mushy.
canh-bap-cai-thit-vien.image_alt: Vietnamese cabbage soup with pork meatballs and carrot.

ingredients.name: Cabbage
ingredients.notes: Rinse and cut into bite-size pieces.

ingredients.name: Ground pork
ingredients.notes: A little fat helps keep meatballs moist.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: Part may be replaced with stock.

preparation_steps: Rinse and cut cabbage and broccoli. Slice the carrot and scallions.
Mix pork with pork paste and shallot, knead until cohesive and shape into balls.
cooking_steps: Bring water to a boil. Add meatballs and simmer gently, skimming the broth.
When nearly cooked, add carrot and broccoli, then cabbage.
Simmer until vegetables are tender, season, add scallions and serve.
canh-bap-cai-thit-vien.media_alt_text: A bowl of cabbage soup with tender meatballs, pale green cabbage and carrot in a clear broth.

canh-bi-xanh-tom-kho.name: Winter Melon Soup with Dried Shrimp
aliases: Winter Gourd Soup with Dried Shrimp
canh-bi-xanh-tom-kho.serving_basis: One light pot for four people.
canh-bi-xanh-tom-kho.description: Winter melon simmered with dried shrimp creates a naturally sweet, gentle broth that pairs well with braised or fried dishes.
canh-bi-xanh-tom-kho.finished_dish: Tender but intact melon pieces and a gently sweet shrimp broth.
canh-bi-xanh-tom-kho.serving: Serve hot with scallions, pepper and rice.
tips: Soak and rinse dried shrimp to soften it and remove grit.
Add scallions after turning off the heat.
canh-bi-xanh-tom-kho.image_alt: Winter melon soup with dried shrimp in clear broth.
canh-bi-xanh-tom-kho.time_note: About 60 minutes, including about 15 minutes to soak the dried shrimp.

ingredients.name: Winter melon
ingredients.notes: Peel, seed if mature and cut into thick pieces.

preparation_steps: Rinse and soak dried shrimp, then lightly pound.
Peel and cut the winter melon; chop shallot and scallions.
cooking_steps: Saute shallot and dried shrimp briefly.
Add water and simmer 10–15 minutes; season lightly.
Add melon and cook until translucent but intact. Finish with scallions.
canh-bi-xanh-tom-kho.media_alt_text: A bowl of winter melon soup with dried shrimp in a clear broth.

ca-doi-kho-me.name: Mullet Braised with Tamarind
ca-doi-kho-me.serving_basis: Four portions of fish to serve with rice.
ca-doi-kho-me.description: Mullet braised with tamarind, fish sauce and aromatics balances sour, sweet and savory flavors. Serve with rice and blanched greens.
ca-doi-kho-me.finished_dish: Firm cooked fish in glossy brown sauce with gentle tamarind acidity, shallot, garlic and pepper.
ca-doi-kho-me.serving: Serve with rice and greens; lift the fish gently to keep it intact.
tips: Clean the belly lining and drain the fish well.
Strain tamarind liquid to remove seeds and fibers.
Braise gently until opaque near the bone.
ca-doi-kho-me.image_alt: Mullet braised with tamarind in a clay pot.

ingredients.name: Ripe tamarind
ingredients.notes: Mash with hot water and strain.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Use some for seasoning and finishing.

ingredients.name: Salt
ingredients.notes: Rub onto the fish, then rinse.

preparation_steps: Clean the fish, rub with salt, rinse, drain and cut into portions.
Mash and strain tamarind. Marinate fish with aromatics, fish sauce, sugar and pepper for about 20 minutes.
cooking_steps: Arrange fish in a pot and heat until the surface firms.
Add tamarind liquid and enough water to partly cover. Simmer gently until cooked through and sauce reduces.
Balance the flavor, add chili, pepper and scallions, then serve with rice.
ca-doi-kho-me.media_alt_text: Mullet braised with tamarind in a clay pot, coated in a glossy brown sauce with shallots, scallions and chili.

com-chien-ca-man.name: Southern Vietnamese Salted Fish Fried Rice
aliases: Vietnamese Fried Rice with Salted Fish
com-chien-ca-man.serving_basis: Four servings for breakfast or a quick main meal.
com-chien-ca-man.description: Day-old rice is stir-fried with shredded salted fish, egg and cabbage. This Southern-style dish makes practical use of leftover rice.
com-chien-ca-man.finished_dish: Hot separate grains with garlic aroma, salted fish, soft egg and lightly crisp cabbage.
com-chien-ca-man.serving: Serve hot with cucumber or pickled vegetables to balance the saltiness.
tips: Pan-fry the fish, remove bones and taste before adding more seasoning.
Fry in batches if the pan is small.
com-chien-ca-man.image_alt: Salted fish fried rice with golden grains, fish, egg, cabbage and scallions.

ingredients.name: Salted dried fish
ingredients.notes: Choose a less bony portion; soak if very salty.

preparation_steps: Separate cooled rice. Rinse fish if very salty, pat dry and pan-fry; remove bones and flake.
Shred cabbage, chop aromatics and beat the eggs.
cooking_steps: Saute aromatics in oil. Add the fish, stir briefly and set aside.
Scramble eggs, add rice and stir until hot and grains separate.
Return fish and cabbage to the pan. Season lightly, add scallions and turn off the heat.
com-chien-ca-man.media_alt_text: A plate of golden fried rice with salted fish, shredded egg, cabbage and scallions.

canh-tom-nam-mong-toi.name: Malabar Spinach Soup with Shrimp Balls and Oyster Mushrooms
aliases: Vietnamese Shrimp Ball and Malabar Spinach Soup
Shrimp, Mushroom and Malabar Spinach Soup
canh-tom-nam-mong-toi.serving_basis: One pot of shrimp-ball soup with greens and mushrooms for four.
canh-tom-nam-mong-toi.description: Fresh shrimp wrapped in pork paste simmers with oyster mushrooms, tomato and Malabar spinach. The light broth has gentle tomato acidity and is served with rice.
canh-tom-nam-mong-toi.finished_dish: Juicy shrimp balls, tender mushrooms, green spinach and a gently sweet broth with mild tomato tang.
canh-tom-nam-mong-toi.serving: Serve hot with rice; cook the greens only until just tender.
tips: Wrap pork paste around each shrimp portion and leave the tail visible.
Saute shrimp heads with aromatics before adding water for a fragrant broth.
Add Malabar spinach last and turn off the heat as it wilts.
canh-tom-nam-mong-toi.image_alt: Malabar spinach soup with shrimp balls, oyster mushrooms and tomato.
canh-tom-nam-mong-toi.time_note: About 35 minutes; add greens near the end.

ingredients.name: Fresh shrimp
ingredients.notes: Peel and devein; reserve heads for broth if desired.

ingredients.name: Malabar spinach
ingredients.notes: Pick and rinse tender leaves and shoots.

ingredients.name: Water
ingredients.notes: May be replaced with strained shrimp-head broth.

ingredients.name: Ground black pepper
ingredients.notes: Use a little in the pork paste and broth.

preparation_steps: Peel and devein shrimp. Reserve heads for broth if desired, and cut bodies into small portions.
Mix pork paste with pepper and a little shallot. Wrap portions around shrimp and leave tails exposed.
Rinse mushrooms and Malabar spinach. Cut greens and tomato.
cooking_steps: Saute shallot and garlic. If using shrimp heads, cook until pink, add water, boil and strain.
Add tomato and mushrooms; simmer briefly. Add shrimp balls and cook until firm and done.
Season, add Malabar spinach and cook just until wilted.
canh-tom-nam-mong-toi.media_alt_text: A bowl of shrimp and Malabar spinach soup with oyster mushrooms, tomato and shrimp-paste balls.
